note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 134, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Exact linked article, named engagement and complete source first/last day match the catalogue. The row is parentless, with no competing source row for this target. Preserve the two original source NAM force identities; counts remain CDB estimates.

The recorded French army in 1809–1814 receives the shako-and-musket infantry family. Musée de l’Armée documents the shako replacing the bicorne from 1806 and surviving 1813–1815 equipment; its evidence supports this later-period component without claiming uniform issue across every regiment or allied contingent. The model is a representative infantry component, not an exact regimental uniform or a statement that every soldier used that equipment. Coalition identities, component proportions, CDB 90 personnel evidence and all loss categories remain unchanged.
